subject.title: Windows: multiple gateway-down failure modes (kill-and-rebind restart loop, config-edit no-relaunch, browser launch crash, blocking pricing fetches)

question: Should maintainers keep this issue as the canonical umbrella and split it into prioritized Windows gateway recovery fixes, or require live Windows repro proof before accepting any scoped implementation work?
rationale: The issue spans stable gateway lifecycle, Windows service supervision, config repair semantics, browser isolation, and pricing startup behavior, so the durable fix order and ownership boundaries need maintainer intent before autonomous code work.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split fixes
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical tracker, prioritize the idempotent lifecycle/config-repair blockers first, and open narrower implementation issues or PRs after live Windows proof confirms the remaining paths.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Pause implementation until a maintainer or QA run reproduces the Scheduled Task relaunch, zombie process, and Edge crash paths on Windows 11 with current main.

options.title: Close subsets only after proof
options.body: Close or supersede only individual sub-modes that are proven fixed on current main while leaving the unresolved Windows recovery blocker tracked here.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split fixes
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the canonical tracker, prioritize the idempotent lifecycle/config-repair blockers first, and open narrower implementation issues or PRs after live Windows proof confirms the remaining paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The current source history points this person at the widest set of gateway lifecycle, config, pricing, and Windows restart files implicated by the umbrella.
